questions.knowledgeNote: Evaluate P(1), P(2), P(3) directly: (n+1)(n+2) is even for n = 1, 2, 3.
questions.question: Q1(a). If P(n) is '(n+1)(n+2) is an odd number', find P(1), P(2), P(3). Are they true?
questions.solution: P(1): 2×3 = 6 (even, not odd — false). P(2): 3×4 = 12 (even — false). P(3): 4×5 = 20 (even — false). None is true: (n+1)(n+2) is always the product of consecutive integers, hence always even.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q1(a); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: 1^3+1 = 2 and 2^3+2 = 10 are both even: both statements true.
questions.question: Q1(b). If P(n) is 'n^3+n is divisible by 2', write P(1) and P(2). Are they true?
questions.solution: P(1): 1+1 = 2, divisible by 2 — true. P(2): 8+2 = 10, divisible by 2 — true.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q1(b); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: P(1): 1 >= 2 is false; P(2), P(3) hold — a statement can fail at n = 1 yet hold later.
questions.question: Q1(c). If P(n) is 'n^2 >= 2^n', show P(1) is false and P(2), P(3) are true.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q1(c); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Base n = 1: 1 = 1·2/2; step adds (m+1) to both sides and factors (m+1)(m+2)/2.
questions.question: Q2(i). By induction: 1+2+3+...+n = n(n+1)/2 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 1 = 1·2/2 ✓. Assume true for m; add (m+1): LHS = m(m+1)/2+(m+1) = (m+1)(m+2)/2, the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n by induction.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q2(i); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(ii). By induction: 1+3+5+...+(2n-1) = n^2 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 1 = 1^2 ✓. Assume true for m; add (2m+1): LHS = m^2+2m+1 = (m+1)^2, the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q2(ii); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(iii). By induction: 2+4+6+...+2n = n(n+1) for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 2 = 1·2 ✓. Assume true for m; add 2(m+1): LHS = m(m+1)+2(m+1) = (m+1)(m+2), the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q2(iii); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(iv). By induction: 2+5+8+...+(3n-1) = n(3n+1)/2 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 2 = 1·4/2 ✓. Assume true for m; add (3m+2): LHS = m(3m+1)/2+(3m+2) = (3m^2+7m+4)/2 = (m+1)(3m+4)/2 = (m+1)(3(m+1)+1)/2, the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q2(iv); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2(v). By induction: 1^2+3^2+5^2+...+(2n-1)^2 = n(2n-1)(2n+1)/3 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 1 = 1·1·3/3 ✓. Assume true for m; add (2m+1)^2: LHS = (2m+1)[m(2m-1)/3+(2m+1)] = (2m+1)(2m^2+5m+3)/3 = (2m+1)(m+1)(2m+3)/3 = (m+1)(2(m+1)-1)(2(m+1)+1)/3, the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q2(v); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Add (m+1)^3 to m^2(m+1)^2/4: perfect square (m+1)^2(m+2)^2/4 emerges.
questions.question: Q2(vi). By induction: 1^3+2^3+3^3+...+n^3 = n^2(n+1)^2/4 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 1 = 1·4/4 ✓. Assume true for m; add (m+1)^3: LHS = (m+1)^2[m^2/4+(m+1)] = (m+1)^2(m+2)^2/4, the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q2(vi); book p236 = PDF p263 (vision read)

questions.question: Q3(i). By induction: 1.2+2.3+3.4+...+n(n+1) = n(n+1)(n+2)/3 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 2 = 1·2·3/3 ✓. Assume true for m; add (m+1)(m+2): LHS = (m+1)(m+2)(m/3+1) = (m+1)(m+2)(m+3)/3, the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q3(i); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)

questions.question: Q3(ii). By induction: 1/(1.2)+1/(2.3)+...+1/(n(n+1)) = n/(n+1) for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 1/2 = 1/2 ✓. Assume true for m; add 1/((m+1)(m+2)) = 1/(m+1)-1/(m+2): LHS = m/(m+1)+1/(m+1)-1/(m+2) = 1-1/(m+2) = (m+1)/(m+2), the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q3(ii); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)

questions.question: Q3(iii). By induction: 1/2+1/4+1/8+...+1/2^n = 1-1/2^n for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 1/2 = 1-1/2 ✓. Assume true for m; add 1/2^{m+1}: LHS = 1-1/2^m+1/2^{m+1} = 1-1/2^{m+1}, the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q3(iii); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)

questions.question: Q3(iv). By induction: 2+2^2+2^3+...+2^n = 2(2^n-1) for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: n = 1 gives 2 = 2(2-1) ✓. Assume true for m; add 2^{m+1}: LHS = 2(2^m-1)+2^{m+1} = 2^{m+2}-2 = 2(2^{m+1}-1), the formula at m+1. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q3(iv); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)

questions.question: Q4(i). Prove by induction that n^2+n is an even number for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: 1+1 = 2, even ✓. Assume m^2+m even; then (m+1)^2+(m+1) = (m^2+m)+2(m+1), even+even = even. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q4(i); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Increment: 3m^2+3m+3 = 3(m^2+m+1), a multiple of 3 on top of the hypothesis.
questions.question: Q4(ii). Prove by induction that n^3+2n is divisible by 3 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: 1+2 = 3 ✓. Assume 3 | m^3+2m; then (m+1)^3+2(m+1) = (m^3+2m)+3m^2+3m+3 = (m^3+2m)+3(m^2+m+1), divisible by 3. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q4(ii); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Of three consecutive integers one is a multiple of 3 (and one even): use (m+1)(m+2)(m+3)-(previous) = 3(m+1)(m+2).
questions.question: Q4(iii). Prove by induction that n(n+1)(n+2) is a multiple of 6 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: 1·2·3 = 6 ✓. Assume 6 | m(m+1)(m+2); then (m+1)(m+2)(m+3) = m(m+1)(m+2)+3(m+1)(m+2). Now (m+1)(m+2) is even (consecutive integers), so 3(m+1)(m+2) is a multiple of 6; adding the hypothesis keeps a multiple of 6. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q4(iii); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: 3^{2(m+1)}-1 = 9·3^{2m}-9+8: split off a multiple of 8 plus 8.
questions.question: Q5(i). By induction prove that 3^{2n}-1 is divisible by 8 for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: 3^2-1 = 8 ✓. Assume 8 | 3^{2m}-1; then 3^{2(m+1)}-1 = 9·3^{2m}-1 = 9(3^{2m}-1)+8, divisible by 8. Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q5(i); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5(ii). By induction prove that x^n-y^n is divisible by x-y for all natural n.
questions.solution: Base: x-y divides itself ✓. Assume (x-y) | x^m-y^m; then x^{m+1}-y^{m+1} = x(x^m-y^m)+y^m(x-y), and both terms are multiples of (x-y). Hence true for all n.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.8 Ex 8.4 Q5(ii); book p237 = PDF p264 (vision read)
